title: Delegate expansion highlight animation does not match content animation
line: When you expand or collapse an item in the Networks, Bluetooth or Disks & Devices popups, the blue highlight now grows and shrinks together with it instead of lagging behind.
explanation: ExpandableListItem animates its own height when it expands or collapses, and the ListView's highlight is meant to follow it. But the view restarts its highlight resize animation (a SmoothedAnimation with the full duration) on every height change, so every frame the highlight starts chasing a new target and stays behind: details are drawn outside the highlight while expanding, and the highlight stays tall after collapsing. Now, while its height animation runs and it is the current item, the item sets the highlight's height itself, so the view's animation has nothing left to do and stops at once.

commits.message:
ExpandableListItem: resize the view's highlight together with the item

While the item animated its height, the list view restarted its own
highlight resize animation on every frame, so the highlight lagged behind
the content when expanding and collapsing. Set its height directly instead.

BUG: 494153

media.caption: Before: consecutive frames (30 fps) of expanding (top row) and collapsing (bottom row) a Wi-Fi network in the Networks popup. The details are drawn below the highlight, and after collapsing the highlight stays tall over empty space.
After: the same frames of expanding and collapsing. The highlight always covers exactly the item.
Before, at quarter speed: the highlight lags behind the content both ways.
After, at quarter speed: highlight and content move together.

review.text: Solid, targeted fix in libplasma's ExpandableListItem.qml addressing the real root cause for all applets that use it. Synchronizing view.highlightItem.height in onHeightChanged while heightAnimation is running happens before QQuickListView::updatePolish() calls updateHighlight(), so the view sees the highlight already at the target height and stops restarting its chasing animation. As a minor non-blocking nitpick, also checking view.highlightFollowsCurrentItem would further guard against clobbering custom highlights, though heightAnimation already requires highlightResizeDuration > 0.
